title: Subsecond metering ledger for dedicated burst (leaky-bucket + backfill)
creator: Anita Shah
description:
Problem: Dedicated capacity customers expect subsecond-accurate burst accounting (leaky-bucket style) and deterministic SLA crediting when nodes transiently lose capacity. Current pipeline aggregates at 1min granularity and runs nightly reconciliations which causes (a) under/overcharging for short bursts, (b) heavy backfill load after node restarts, and (c) opaque SLA credit calculations.

Goal: Design and implement a subsecond, event-sourced metering ledger for dedicated pools that: (1) allows per-tenant leaky-bucket counters with configurable reservation guarantees, (2) records bursts atomically so short high-throughput spikes are billed correctly, (3) supports idempotent backfill corrections for missed events due to transient failures, and (4) produces deterministic SLA credit reports (explainable to customer success) with audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant leaky-bucket counters emit usage events at <=1s granularity for 99% of requests
Event-sourced ledger persisted in append-only store with idempotent write keys and event sequencing
Backfill job can reconcile and correct missed events without double-billing (safe run twice semantics)
SLA credit calculation matches manual spot-checks across 10 representative tenants with varied burst patterns
End-to-end tests covering node failover, delayed events, and concurrent bursts included in CI
technical_notes: Use existing streaming ingestion (kafka topic 'metering.dedicated.events') as primary input; augment with event type 'LEAKY_BUCKET_TICK' emitted by runtime at request commit path
Ledger store: implement append-only partitioned ledger in CockroachDB using partition key (tenant_id, date) with event_seq for idempotency. Avoid wide transactions by batching commits per-second.

Burst model: per-tenant bucket with capacity=reserved_throughput*burst_multiplier; leak rate = reserved_throughput. Token credits consumed on request commit. If insufficient tokens, request billed against burst pool and flagged for pro-rata allocation and potential throttling based on policy.

Backfill strategy: runtime writes tombstone placeholders for events during node restart window. Backfill job replays runtime logs and reconciles ledger using event_seq to insert missing events; ledger logic enforces deduplication by event_id to maintain idempotency.

SLA credits: compute rolling SLA shortfalls from ledger events and produce time-windowed deficits. Credit rules: proportional to reserved throughput shortfall per-hour, capped by contractual limits. We will store both raw deficit seconds and dollar-equivalent for downstream billing.
Performance: aim for <5% CPU overhead on serving path by offloading heavy serialization to async workers; sampling mode for low-volume tenants to reduce throughput pressure.
Observability: emit metrics for 'metering.events.ingested', 'ledger.write.latency', 'backfill.corrections_applied', and per-tenant discrepancy deltas; expose traces to Console for investigations.
decisions: Chosen an event-sourced ledger instead of periodic counters to guarantee deterministic corrections and auditability
Persist ledger in CockroachDB (consistent transactional semantics) rather than a pure log because we need indexed queries for per-tenant SLA reports
Keep per-second commit granularity instead of sub-second to balance write amplification vs accuracy; runtime will aggregate micro-events into per-second batches before emitting to Kafka
Backfill will be conservative: prefer under-billing (issue refunds/credits) to avoid double-charging customers
comments: 2026-02-26 - Anita S.: Kickoff meeting with runtime and billing. Agreed on event schema and minimum fields (event_id, tenant_id, timestamp, tokens_consumed, reserved_capacity_ref, origin_node). Action: Marco to prototype emitter in runtime.
2026-03-02 - Marco L.: Prototype emitter implemented; emits per-second aggregated LEAKY_BUCKET_TICK events to Kafka. Observed 1.8ms median overhead on request path in local stress tests.
2026-03-04 - Sarah K. (Billing): Reviewed event model and asked for explicit 'billing_reason' field for audits. Added to schema and updated Confluence.

2026-03-07 - Reliability: Simulated node restart; runtime emitted tombstones but backfill job initially failed due to missing event_seq handling. Fixed dedupe logic and re-ran backfill; ledger corrected 7 tenants with small deficits.

2026-03-11 - Legal/Finance sync: Agreed to surface provisional SLA credit amounts in billing UI 7 days before invoice to allow customer dispute window. Finance requested CSV export format for credits.

2026-03-13 - Marco L.: Integration PR opened (infra#4782). Running cluster-wide canary on staging for 72h; monitoring backfill corrections and ledger write latency. Next: add end-to-end tests and roll out to limited Dedicated pools.
